title: Lagarde Calls for Diversification of Central Africa’s Resources

image.attribution: IMF Staff Photo/Stephen Jaffe / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
International Monetary Fund chief Christine Lagarde urged central African states to diversify their economies, which have been hit by plummeting petroleum prices and terrorism. The IMF managing director’s three-day visit to Cameroon comes at a time when the war against terrorism and the crisis in the Central African Republic have negatively impacted the region’s economies.

Christine Lagarde says although all six central African states counted on their petroleum resources to improve their economies, Gabon, Chad and Equatorial Guinea have suffered most as a result of reducing world prices. She says they did not diversify their economies like Cameroon did.

Alamine Ousman Mey, Cameroon’s minister of finance, says in spite of the challenges, his country’s economy has shown some resiliency because of the diversification that developed value chains in agriculture, the construction sector and energy supply.

International oil prices have more than halved between 2014 and 2015, making it very difficult for the region where five out of its six member nations are oil producers. Additionally, terrorist threats that spilled over from Nigeria to Cameroon and Chad disturbed economic activity and generated additional budgetary spending.

questions.question: What does Christine Lagarde think that central African states should do?
What events have had a big negative impact on these economies?
options: Rising foreign investments and growth in the tourism sector
Increased trade agreements with neighboring countries
Technological advancements in the energy sector

questions.question: Which countries in the area are suffering the most because of low oil prices?
options: Central African Republic and Equatorial Guinea
